title: Spatial organization of heterogeneities in the striatum
title_zh: 纹状体中异质性的空间组织
abstract: The striatum is usually described through a binary taxonomy of D1/D2 spiny projection neurons and coarse basal ganglia pathways supporting action selection and reinforcement learning. Yet the striatum is also a recurrent inhibitory network with strong neuromodulatory control, and its cellular and synaptic properties are not uniformly distributed. Spatial transcriptomics reveal continuous gradients in gene expression across striatal territory, superimposed on the discrete striosome-matrix division. Other studies report that intrinsic properties (such as excitability), inhibitory interneuron abundance and neuromodulatory fields (e.g. terminal distribution, clearance kinetics, receptor expression) vary in space. These spatially structured heterogeneities seem to align with striatal topographic input and output maps, suggesting that its computation cannot be uniformly distributed as well. We propose that the striatum is best understood as a spatial dynamical field, meaning that neighboring striatal microcircuits have similar but not identical dynamical properties and these position-dependent parameters shape network dynamics affecting integration, competition, and plasticity differently in the striatal tissue.
